# Alloy Forge extension API (v1.0)

For people writing a package. The design is in [EXTENSIONS_SPEC.md](EXTENSIONS_SPEC.md); this file is the reference. Forge API version: **1.0**. A package says which API it was written for in `forgeApi` (`"^1.0"`: same major version, host minor at least that).

## One format, two tiers

A package is a `.alloyext` file (a zip) with `alloy-extension.json` at its root. **What a package asks for decides its tier**; authors never pick it.

- **Plugin**: only the permissions marked `plugin` below. Runs in one Web Worker with no DOM. For feature types, checks, importers/exporters, libraries, AI tools and loop steps.
- **Extension**: asks for any permission marked `extension` (a pane, an overlay, the GPU, the runner, or a network host). Its own Worker, plus sandboxed iframes for panes.

The install prompt shows the tier and every permission in words ("Plugin: reads and edits your design", "Extension: runs its own code on your GPU / talks to <host>").

## Manifest

```json
{
  "id": "xyz.example.thing",
  "name": "Thing",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "forgeApi": "^1.0",
  "author": "You",
  "licence": "PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0",
  "main": "main.js",
  "permissions": ["doc.read", "checks"],
  "contributes": { "checks": [{ "id": "my-check", "label": "My check" }] },
  "integrity": "sha256-…"
}
```

The schema is `MANIFEST_SCHEMA` in `src/ext/manifest.js` (plain JSON Schema). Beyond the schema the loader enforces: every permission is known (`network:<host>` names one exact host; no wildcards), a `contributes` kind needs its permission (table below), ids are unique, `main` and pane files exist, and `forgeApi` is supported.

### Permissions

| Permission | Tier | The package may |
|---|---|---|
| `doc.read` | plugin | read your design (parameters, features, bodies, PCB data) |
| `doc.ops` | plugin | edit your design through typed ops (validated, lock-checked, undoable) |
| `geometry.read` | plugin | read the built geometry (meshes, B-rep, voxels) |
| `checks` | plugin | add rows to the check scorecard and the design loop |
| `agent.tools` | plugin | give the AI assistant and the MCP server new tools |
| `loop` | plugin | add steps to the design loop |
| `storage` | plugin | keep its own settings in the project and in this browser |
| `ui.pane` | extension | show its own pane (a sandboxed page with no network) |
| `scene.overlay` | extension | draw overlays in the 3D viewport |
| `compute.gpu` | extension | run compute on your GPU (WebGPU) |
| `compute.remote` | extension | talk to the Alloy Runner URL you entered in Settings |
| `network:<host>` | extension | make network requests to the named host only |

### Contributions

| `contributes` kind | Needs permission |
|---|---|
| `featureTypes` | none |
| `templates` | `doc.ops` |
| `stylePacks` | none |
| `checks` | `checks` |
| `analyses` | `doc.read` |
| `exporters` | `geometry.read` |
| `importers` | `doc.ops` |
| `libraries` | `doc.ops` |
| `agentTools` | `agent.tools` |
| `loopSteps` | `loop` |
| `panes` | `ui.pane` |
| `overlays` | `scene.overlay` |
| `settings` | none |

A feature type is declared with its fields so Forge can show it before your code runs:

```json
"featureTypes": [{ "id": "rib", "label": "Rib", "icon": "▮", "fields": [
  { "k": "length", "kind": "num", "def": "20" }, { "k": "axis", "kind": "enum", "opts": ["x", "y"], "def": "x" },
  { "k": "pos", "kind": "vec3", "def": ["0", "0", "0"] } ] }]
```

Field kinds: `num` (an expression, evaluated for you), `vec3`, `enum`, `text`. `name`, `body`, `op`, `id`, `type`, `ext`, `suppressed` and `locked` are reserved. Features are saved as `type: "<package id>/<type id>"` with `ext: "<package id>"`.

### Integrity

`integrity` is `"sha256-" + hex(sha256(…))` over every file sorted by path, each as `path\0 hex(sha256(bytes))\n`, where `alloy-extension.json` is hashed as canonical JSON (keys sorted) without its own `integrity` field. It ties the manifest (and so the permissions) to the exact files: a package edited after it was built, or whose permissions were widened, is refused. It is **not** a signature and does not say who made it. `node tools/pack-ext.mjs <dir> <out.alloyext>` computes it for you.

## Writing the code

`main.js` is a classic script. Forge calls it once in a Worker with two globals: `forge` (the API below) and `console` (captured, shown in Settings > Extensions). It is not an ES module: no `import`, no `require`; put everything in the file or in files you read yourself.

```js
// plugin: a feature type is a recipe that returns built-in features
forge.featureType.register('rib', {
  expand(v) { return [{ type: 'box', size: [v.length, v.thickness, v.height], anchor: 'bottom', pos: v.pos }]; },
});
// a check reads the design and returns a scorecard row
forge.checks.register('rib-thickness', async () => {
  const doc = await forge.doc.get();
  return { pass: true, detail: 'ok', validity: 'estimate' };
});
```

**Feature types never produce geometry.** `expand(values, ctx)` receives your fields evaluated to numbers and returns an array (at most 64) of built-in feature specs: `box`, `cylinder`, `sphere`, `slot`, `hole`, `standoff` and the other primitives (not `import`, `split` or the OCCT-only types). Each spec is validated like any feature, gets your feature's body and (unless it sets `op`) operation, and is built by the kernel. Results are cached by package, type and values.

**Checks** return `{ pass: boolean, detail?: string, items?: any[], validity?: "estimate" | "validated" | "experimental" }`. `experimental` rows are shown but never decide the verdict. A check that throws, times out (20 s) or returns something else is a failing row, not a silent pass.

**Long work**: `run(input, { progress, signal })` and every host call take an `AbortSignal`; call `progress(0..1)` often. Check `signal.aborted` in loops. The host can also stop a Worker that does not answer (30 s default; E_TIMEOUT) and restarts it on next use.

## Panes

A pane is an HTML file from your package (`contributes.panes[].file`), shown in a sandboxed iframe: `sandbox="allow-scripts"`, an opaque origin, and a CSP of `default-src 'none'` (inline script and style only; `<script src>` and `<link rel=stylesheet>` that point at files in your package are inlined for you). It has no network and cannot touch Forge. It talks to your Worker only:

```js
// in the pane
const out = await alloy.call('scan', { max: 4000 });  // -> your Worker
alloy.on('message', (m) => { /* from forge.ui.pane.post */ });
alloy.on('theme', (t) => { /* { ink, dim, acc, dark } */ });
// in main.js
forge.ui.pane.onCall(async (paneId, method, data) => { /* return a value */ });
```

## API reference

### `forge.doc.get`

```ts
forge.doc.get() → Project (JSON). Asset bytes are left out.
```

- Permission: `doc.read`

The current design document.

### `forge.doc.applyOps`

```ts
forge.doc.applyOps(ops: Op[]) → { log: string[] }
```

- Permission: `doc.ops`

Apply typed ops to the design. The host runs the same `applyOps` the AI uses: ops are validated, locks are enforced, and the whole call is one undoable step. A rejected op rejects the call and changes nothing. A package cannot enable or disable extensions, and `ext_set` is limited to its own id.

### `forge.pcb.get`

```ts
forge.pcb.get() → PcbBlock
```

- Permission: `doc.read`

The `pcb` block of the document (components, cutouts, supports, keep regions).

### `forge.geometry.list`

```ts
forge.geometry.list() → { name, ref: boolean, bbox, volume_mm3, tris }[]
```

- Permission: `geometry.read`

The bodies and reference parts of the current build (hidden bodies included).

### `forge.geometry.mesh`

```ts
forge.geometry.mesh(body: string) → { positions: Float32Array, indices: Uint32Array, bbox, volume_mm3 }
```

- Permission: `geometry.read`

Triangle mesh of a built body or reference part, in millimetres.

### `forge.geometry.brep`

```ts
forge.geometry.brep(body: string) → { step: Uint8Array }
```

- Permission: `geometry.read`

STEP bytes of a body. Only on the OCCT kernel; on Manifold the call rejects with E_UNAVAILABLE.

### `forge.geometry.voxelize`

```ts
forge.geometry.voxelize(body: string, h: number, opts?: { maxVoxels?: number }) → { origin: number[3], h: number, dims: number[3], data: Uint8Array }
```

- Permission: `geometry.read`

Fill a body into a regular grid (1 = inside). CPU reference implementation; refuses grids over `maxVoxels` (default 4 000 000, hard cap 8 000 000) with E_LIMIT. A GPU version replaces it in A2 behind the same call.

### `forge.checks.register`

```ts
forge.checks.register(id: string, fn: (input: { project, bodies }, ctx) => CheckRow | Promise<CheckRow>) → void
```

- Permission: `checks`
- Must be declared in `contributes.checks`
- Registration: the function stays in your Worker; the host calls it when needed

Add a check. `id` must be declared in `contributes.checks`. `fn(input, ctx)` receives `input = { project, bodies }`: the design being checked (in the design loop that is the candidate, which may differ from the open document, so use `input.project` rather than `forge.doc.get()`) and a summary of its build (`name, ref, bbox, volume_mm3, tris`). It returns `{ pass, detail, items?, validity? }`. A row with `validity: "experimental"` is shown but never gates a pass/fail verdict.

### `forge.analysis.register`

```ts
forge.analysis.register(id: string, impl: { run(input, ctx), cancel?() }) → void
```

- Permission: `doc.read`
- Must be declared in `contributes.analyses`
- Registration: the function stays in your Worker; the host calls it when needed

`id` must be declared in `contributes.analyses`. `run(input, { progress, signal })` returns an AnalysisResult (docs/EXTENSIONS_SPEC.md section 3.3). Runs in the package Worker; the host can cancel it.

### `forge.featureType.register`

```ts
forge.featureType.register(id: string, impl: { expand(values, ctx) }) → void
```

- Permission: none
- Must be declared in `contributes.featureTypes`
- Registration: the function stays in your Worker; the host calls it when needed

A feature type is a recipe: `expand` receives the evaluated fields and returns built-in feature specs (box, cylinder, hole, ...). The kernel builds those; the package never produces geometry itself. Fields are declared in the manifest.

### `forge.agent.tool`

```ts
forge.agent.tool(id: string, fn: (args, ctx) => any) → void
```

- Permission: `agent.tools`
- Must be declared in `contributes.agentTools`
- Registration: the function stays in your Worker; the host calls it when needed

Expose a tool to the in-app AI and the MCP server. `id` must be declared in `contributes.agentTools` with a JSON Schema for its arguments.

### `forge.loop.step`

```ts
forge.loop.step(id: string, fn: (ctx) => any) → void
```

- Permission: `loop`
- Must be declared in `contributes.loopSteps`
- Registration: the function stays in your Worker; the host calls it when needed

A step the design loop can call. `id` must be declared in `contributes.loopSteps`.

### `forge.scene.overlay`

```ts
forge.scene.overlay(id: string, overlay: Overlay) → void
```

- Permission: `scene.overlay`
- Must be declared in `contributes.overlays`

Draw or replace an overlay. Kinds: `points` ({ positions: Float32Array, values: Float32Array, unit, label, range? }) and `box` ({ min, max, label }). The host adds the colour map, legend and tap probe. `id` must be declared in `contributes.overlays`.

### `forge.scene.clearOverlay`

```ts
forge.scene.clearOverlay(id: string) → void
```

- Permission: `scene.overlay`

Remove an overlay.

### `forge.ui.pane.open`

```ts
forge.ui.pane.open(id: string) → void
```

- Permission: `ui.pane`
- Must be declared in `contributes.panes`

Show a pane declared in `contributes.panes`. A pane is an HTML file from the package, loaded in a sandboxed iframe (`allow-scripts` only, no network, no same-origin).

### `forge.ui.pane.post`

```ts
forge.ui.pane.post(id: string, message: any) → void
```

- Permission: `ui.pane`
- Must be declared in `contributes.panes`

Send a message to an open pane. The pane replies through `alloy.call` / `alloy.on` (see EXTENSION_API.md, "Panes").

### `forge.ui.pane.onCall`

```ts
forge.ui.pane.onCall(fn: (paneId, method, data) => any) → void
```

- Permission: none (runs in the Worker)

Local: handle calls a pane makes with `alloy.call(method, data)`. The return value goes back to the pane. No host round trip.

### `forge.storage.project.get`

```ts
forge.storage.project.get(key: string) → any
```

- Permission: `storage`

Read `project.ext[<id>][key]`.

### `forge.storage.project.set`

```ts
forge.storage.project.set(key: string, value: any) → void
```

- Permission: `storage`

Write `project.ext[<id>][key]` through the `ext_set` op, so it is saved with the project and is undoable. Values up to 256 KB.

### `forge.storage.user.get`

```ts
forge.storage.user.get(key: string) → any
```

- Permission: `storage`

Per-browser storage, private to the package.

### `forge.storage.user.set`

```ts
forge.storage.user.set(key: string, value: any) → void
```

- Permission: `storage`

Values up to 256 KB.

### `forge.compute.gpu.info`

```ts
forge.compute.gpu.info() → { available: boolean, adapter?: string, limits?: object }
```

- Permission: `compute.gpu`

Whether WebGPU is available. `navigator.gpu` is only present inside the Worker of a package that holds `compute.gpu`.

### `forge.compute.remote.fetch`

```ts
forge.compute.remote.fetch(path: string, init?: { method, headers, body }) → { status, headers, body: Uint8Array }
```

- Permission: `compute.remote`

Request to the Alloy Runner URL entered in Settings. `path` must start with `/`. The host adds the runner token; the package never sees it. Rejects with E_UNAVAILABLE when no runner is set.

### `forge.net.fetch`

```ts
forge.net.fetch(url: string, init?: { method, headers, body }) → { status, headers, body: Uint8Array }
```

- Permission: `network:<host>` for the URL's host

Request to a host the package declared as `network:<host>` (exact host name, https, or http on localhost). Anything else is refused.

## Errors

Rejections carry `error.code`:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_PERM` | The package did not declare the permission this call needs. |
| `E_CONTRIB` | The id is not declared in the manifest `contributes`. |
| `E_ARG` | Invalid arguments. |
| `E_UNAVAILABLE` | Not available right now (wrong kernel, no runner, no GPU, ...). |
| `E_LIMIT` | A size or count limit was exceeded. |
| `E_OPS` | The ops were rejected (validation or a lock). Nothing was changed. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | The package Worker did not answer in time and was stopped. |
| `E_CANCELLED` | Cancelled. |

## Security model

What is a hard boundary, and what is not:

- **A Worker has no DOM and no access to the page.** Everything privileged is a message to the host, and the host checks your manifest on **every** call: the permission, then that what you register is declared in `contributes`. There is no other way to read the design, change it, or reach the viewport.
- **Geometry changes are typed ops.** `doc.applyOps` runs the same `applyOps` as the AI: validated, lock-checked, one undoable step, all or nothing. A package can neither install or enable extensions nor write another package's storage. Feature types return feature specs, never meshes.
- **Network is the host's job.** Packages have no `fetch`. `net.fetch` reaches only hosts named in `network:<host>` (https, or http on localhost; redirects are refused so a response cannot send you elsewhere). `compute.remote.fetch` reaches only the runner URL the user entered, and the host adds the runner token: a package never sees it. A package cannot read the AI provider key.
- **Best effort, not a boundary:** before your code runs, the Worker bootstrap deletes network and storage globals (`fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`, `importScripts`, `indexedDB`, nested `Worker`, `navigator.gpu` unless granted) and Forge's page sets a Content-Security-Policy whose `script-src` allows only its own origin and blob: URLs, so a package cannot load code from another origin (`import()`, external workers). The policy still allows `eval` because the STEP reader needs it, and it does not restrict `connect-src` because you choose the AI endpoint. A Worker started from a blob shares the page's origin, so this is defence in depth; a determined malicious package may find a way round it. Install packages you trust, as with any extension. Hardening (running Workers from an opaque-origin iframe) is on the roadmap.
- **Integrity is not authenticity** (see Integrity above). There is no signing or marketplace yet.
- **No telemetry**: nothing in the host reports anything anywhere.

## Limits

Package: 24 MB zipped, 256 files, 12 MB per file, 32 MB expanded, zip64 and encryption refused. Values stored through `storage`: 256 KB. `doc.applyOps`: 200 ops per call. Overlays: 2 000 000 points. `net.fetch` / `compute.remote.fetch` responses: 20 MB. `geometry.voxelize`: 4 000 000 voxels by default, 8 000 000 hard.

## Packing and trying a package

```
node tools/pack-ext.mjs examples/ext/sample-rib dist/ext-samples/sample-rib.alloyext
```

Open Settings > Extensions, choose the file (or paste a URL, or pick a sample), read the install prompt, install, and switch it on for the project. Two samples ship in `examples/ext/`: `sample-rib` (a plugin: a Rib feature type and a check) and `sample-probe` (an extension: a pane and an overlay).

## When a package is removed

The project keeps everything the package made. Its features stay in the file untouched, marked "needs <name>", skipped in builds with a visible warning; its checks show as "needs <name>" rows that do not gate. Installing the package again restores them. Analysis results are never saved in the project (only setups are).
